evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Realign this leaf so its scope is a subset of its parent's contract: re-parent it under epic 061c (which owns prompt caching / cost via its Approach and cache-token AC) or another ticket whose plan contains a token-cost/caching-of-the-overlap-judge deliverable, rather than under the closed class-routing bug afeb whose contract contains none of this work.
evidence: Parent afeb title: 'Hand-built LLM sub-calls bypass the model-class config and go to direct Anthropic' — its whole contract is provider/class ROUTING.

afeb ACs are all model-class selection ('each of the THREE hand-built sub-call sites selects its model from the class vocabulary'; 'a test fails if ANY hand-built sub-call inherits cfg.model while a class table is configured') plus the fail-safe preservation AC — none mentions token cost, caching, or prompt payload.

Leaf title/Context: 'Cut the overlap step's token cost: hoist the shared query digest into the cacheable system prefix'; 'rebar review-plan spends the majority of its input tokens in the Stage-2 overlap judge.' This is a caching/cost concern absent from afeb.
afeb references overlap-judge only as 'the VOLUME site (18 of 23 calls)' being put on the standard class — never as a token/caching target.

Epic 061c (afeb's parent) Approach and its AC 'A gate run ... reports a non-zero cache_read_tokens ...' explicitly own prompt caching and cost — the leaf's concern is a subset of the EPIC, not of afeb.

The leaf does NOT contradict any specific afeb AC: it preserves afeb's standard-class binding and both fail-safes (Scope: 'both fail-safes ... are preserved unedited'), so the divergence is additive out-of-contract scope, not a per-AC contradiction or a required-site omission.
findings.finding: The leaf's scope (hoist the query digest into the cacheable system prefix to cut the overlap step's token cost) is not a subset of its parent afeb's declared scope. Parent afeb (closed bug) is exclusively about routing hand-built LLM sub-calls through the model-class vocabulary; none of its ACs, its Scope, or its Not-in-scope touches token cost, prompt caching, or the shape/size of the overlap judge's prompt payload. The leaf introduces a prompt-caching/token-cost concern the parent's plan does not contain — additive work outside afeb's contract, not consistent narrowing of it. The concern's natural home is the epic 061c, whose Approach and S3 acceptance criterion explicitly own prompt caching and cost.
findings.location: Whole leaf (title / Context / Approach / Scope) vs parent afeb (afeb-bc04-3265-4747) description + ACs
scenarios: A reviewer verifying the leaf against its declared parent afeb finds none of the leaf's deliverables (system-prefix hoist, verdict-parity run, cache-token measurement) traceable to any afeb clause.
afeb is closed and completion-verified; attaching new caching work under it cannot re-open or re-scope a closed bug's contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-parent the leaf to epic 061c (or a live caching/cost story beneath it) whose declared contract already covers prompt caching and input-token cost; keep the afeb reference as a `discovered_from`/`relates_to` prerequisite link ('after afeb landed, overlap-judge runs on standard') rather than as the parent contract.

findings.finding: The plan's 'never worse — identical bytes, moved' claim is inaccurate and its behavioral-equivalence assumption is untested: the AFTER user block replaces the query digest with a cross-block reference pointer, a semantic input change to a precision-sensitive judge that no test validates leaves verdicts unchanged.
findings.location: Approach section ('The relocation is therefore never worse — identical bytes'); Testing/Acceptance Criteria

findings.finding: The overlap-judge base prompt still tells the model both digests arrive together in the user message, but the plan hoists the query digest into the system prompt without reconciling that framing, and leaves the load-bearing 'one-line orientation' / reference-slot wiring unspecified — an instruction-locality gap the directional 'FIRST <relation> SECOND' semantics depend on.
findings.location: Approach (system/user layout sketch) and Scope ('a module-private helper builds the augmented system prompt'); vs src/rebar/llm/reviewers/overlap_judge.md:11-13
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Scope an explicit edit to overlap_judge.md (or the helper's appended header) that (a) names the system digest as one of the two ordered participants and (b) instructs the model to treat 'the QUERY TICKET DIGEST given in your system prompt' as occupying whichever FIRST/SECOND slot the user message places it in; and give the verbatim orientation string rather than a placeholder.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Retitle the ticket to reflect the plan's actual (measured) framing — it lands the structural precondition for caching, not a token-cost cut — so the title no longer contradicts the +4.4% measured increase the body reports.
evidence: Title: 'Cut the overlap step's token cost: hoist the shared query digest into the cacheable system prefix'
Body: '16,748 input tokens versus the baseline's 16,040 — a +708 token (+4.4%) increase'
Body: 'A net token INCREASE is a valid outcome and must be recorded as a regression in plain terms, not presented as a win.'
findings.finding: The title claims a token-cost CUT, but the plan's own real-API measurement shows a token INCREASE (+708 tokens / +4.4%); the title advertises an outcome the body refutes.
scenarios: A reader skims the title and expects a cost reduction, contradicting the measured regression the plan documents.
AC6 requires reporting a regression 'not presented as a win' — the title itself presents it as a win.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to something like 'Hoist the shared query digest into the cacheable system prefix (structural precondition for caching the overlap judge)'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the title with the measured outcome — retitle to reflect the structural-precondition intent (e.g. 'Hoist the shared query digest into the cacheable system prefix to make the overlap step cacheable') rather than promising a cost cut the plan itself refutes.
evidence: Title: 'Cut the overlap step's token cost: hoist the shared query digest into the cacheable system prefix'
Body: '16,748 input tokens versus the baseline's 16,040 — a +708 token (+4.4%) increase'
Body: 'A net token INCREASE is a valid outcome and must be recorded as a regression in plain terms, not presented as a win.'
findings.finding: The title promises to 'Cut the overlap step's token cost', but the plan's own real-API measurement shows the change INCREASES input tokens by +708 (+4.4%) because the hoisted prefix (728-875 tokens) never reaches the 1024 cacheable floor, so no caching occurs. The headline verb 'Cut' is contradicted by the delivered end state.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the ticket to name the actual deliverable (making the shared digest cacheable / a structural precondition for caching) instead of 'Cut ... token cost', since the body proves a net increase at the current prefix size.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate the plan's goal/title so it names what this change actually delivers — the structural precondition for caching this call site (digest moved into the cacheable stable block) — rather than a token-cost cut the plan's own measurement shows it does not achieve until the prefix clears the 1024 floor.
evidence: Title: 'Cut the overlap step's token cost: hoist the shared query digest into the cacheable system prefix'
Plan measurement: 'cache_read_tokens: 0, cache_write_tokens: 0, and 16,748 input tokens versus the baseline's 16,040 — a +708 token (+4.4%) increase'
Plan's own reframe: 'The hoist is the structural precondition for any caching of this call site' and 'A net token INCREASE is a valid outcome and must be recorded as a regression'
This is a fitness-for-purpose (does-it-solve-the-named-problem) observation, not a mechanism defect: the mechanism is sound but the named goal is a proxy the change does not achieve as titled.
findings.finding: The plan's stated goal/title ('Cut the overlap step's token cost') is contradicted by the plan's own measured outcome: a +708 token (+4.4%) INCREASE, because the hoisted prefix (728-875 tokens) sits below the model's 1024-token cache floor and therefore caches nothing. The plan's body reframes the deliverable honestly as 'the structural precondition for any caching' with a strong positive rationale, but the headline goal still names a cost cut this change does not deliver.
findings.location: Title / 'Context / Problem' / 'Why land it anyway' paragraph
scenarios: A reviewer or future reader scanning the title/goal alone concludes the step now costs less, when it costs slightly more until the prefix reaches the floor.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to something like 'Make the overlap judge's shared query digest cacheable: hoist it into the stable system prefix (precondition for caching; does not yet clear the token floor)', and adjust the Context/Problem framing to lead with the precondition-not-savings goal.
